newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian president, PM row over interior ministry.
newsitem.headline: Albanian president, PM row over interior ministry.

text.p: Albania's Socialist-led interim government accused President Sali Berisha on Wednesday of resisting attempts to take control of the interior ministry and its security forces.

Government spokesman Vladimir Prela said Berisha, whose Democratic Party has admitted losing to the Socialists in Sunday's general election, had tried overnight to block the government's appointment of a new Socialist acting interior minister.

Armed groups confronted each other into the early hours of the morning around Tirana's central Skanderbeg Square, but it was impossible to identify which institutions they represented. No shots were fired and the groups later dispersed.
Prela said unidentified troops had also surrounded the prime minister's office for a time during the night.
"Berisha was extremely nervous," he told reporters. "It took several hours of frantic telephone calls to calm matters down. The ministry is completely under the control of the government."
There was no one available at Berisha's office to comment.

Socialist leader Fatos Nano told reporters on Tuesday that Interior Minister Belul Celo, a member of Berisha's defeated Democratic Party, had fled the country and was being replaced as acting minister by a Socialist appointee.
Police armoured vehicles then roared through central Tirana in a show of force.
Prela produced what he said was an order issued by Berisha for units of the elite republican guard to block all approach roads to Tirana as well as the central bank.
An order subsequently issued by Prime Minister Bashkim Fino effectively told troops to ignore the president's instructions.
Prela said Berisha wanted Celo to be replaced by Azem Hajdari, one of the president's most loyal supporters within the Democratic Party.
"The prime minister insists that it is up to the government, not the president, to propose ministerial appointments," Prela said. "It is then up to the president to approve them."
Albania's interim multi-party government was appointed in March when Berisha was forced to call last Sunday's early election to quell country-wide violence.
Berisha went on television earlier this week to concede that his Democrats had been beaten into opposition but has not indicated whether he intends to step down.

Partial results in the slow count give the Socialists a big lead, though many contests will have to go through to a run-off round on Sunday where no candidate won the 50 percent required for outright victory.
The Socialists have called the first authorised rally for Wednesday evening, between the two rounds of the election.
